discoveries.label: Enter the First Floor
discoveries.description: Broad carved descent to a marble landing and enormous arched Kua-tin doors. Beyond them, the first-floor route begins; exact chamber dimensions are unknown.

discoveries.label: Survive the Murder Dozer ambush
discoveries.description: A misleading neon guild sign leads into the goblin Murder Dozer ambush. The alley and trap are one encounter sequence, not two separate destinations.

discoveries.label: Receive the tutorial briefing
discoveries.description: The real Tutorial Guild entrance opens to Mordecai’s personal tutorial space, with a classroom and living area. Mordecai is a guide and NPC here, not a deployable party member.

discoveries.label: Map a route through the First Floor
discoveries.description: A compact playable abstraction of the branching rock-hewn grid. Broad torchlit arteries connect neighborhoods; some side passages use dark red brick and green growth. This is a connector region, not a claim about exact route geometry.

discoveries.label: Resolve the Hoarder encounter
discoveries.description: A round, high-ceiling room among rubbish piles and burst bags, with a grimy signed door and skull torches. The Scatterer territory belongs to this lair complex.

discoveries.label: Find Tally’s safe room
discoveries.description: A Polish fast-food restaurant repurposed as a protected safe room. The children’s play area is inside this same venue. Exact chain branding and layout are not established. Optional route lead; supplies are a tactical adaptation.

discoveries.label: Resolve the goblin workshop encounter
discoveries.description: A goblin engineering and explosives workshop connected to the War Chieftain’s chamber. Workshop equipment is an adaptation of its stated use; exact machinery and room plan are not canonical.

discoveries.label: Explore the DMV safe room
discoveries.description: An Earth DMV waiting room used as a safe room, with curtained cots and an experience-cookie encounter associated with Frank and Maggie. Optional route lead; supplies are a tactical adaptation.

discoveries.label: Resolve the Juicer encounter
discoveries.description: A high-ceiling gym with sliding glass entry, reception turnstile, weights, benches and mats. Red combat lighting is part of the encounter presentation.

discoveries.label: Resolve the Ball of Swine boss encounter
discoveries.description: Rounded tunnels spiral around a courtyard, with portcullises and three bridge approaches. The final boss encounter reveals the arena and its stairwell. The switch chamber and Speedbump construction area are subregions/states, not separate destinations.

discoveries.label: Hear reports of other rest stops
discoveries.description: The guide or crawlers mention an Alabama Waffle House and a candy-vending rest area. This is a report/rumor interaction at the Tutorial Guild, not a physical map destination; neither place is established as a Carl visit. Optional route lead; supplies are a tactical adaptation.

discoveries.label: Visit Meadow Lark’s camp
discoveries.description: A survivor encampment near the borough-boss stairwell. Treat its footprint as an authored camp layout; sources establish the camp and proximity, not a canonical settlement plan. Optional route lead; supplies are a tactical adaptation.

discoveries.label: Find Sebastian’s safe room
discoveries.description: A converted restaurant safe room with kitchen, sleeping area, bathrooms, coffee, and Peruvian beer. Exact room layout is not established. Optional route lead; supplies are a tactical adaptation.

discoveries.label: Unoccupied creature den
discoveries.description: Tucked-away generic nook with sparse crate/barrel/torch dressing. It holds an optional supply cache; no creature, resident or enemy encounter is implied. Optional, procedurally placed game adaptation; exact rooms and supplies are invented.

discoveries.label: Workshop storage annex
discoveries.description: A small workbench-and-crate nook next to the goblin workshop, used as generated set dressing and optional cache space. Optional, procedurally placed game adaptation; exact rooms and supplies are invented.

discoveries.label: Resting nook
discoveries.description: Bench-and-cot alcove beside an established safe-room district. It holds an optional supply cache; it is not protected and has no camp/resume behavior. Optional, procedurally placed game adaptation; exact rooms and supplies are invented.

discoveries.label: Unmarked supply recess
discoveries.description: Small unmarked niche with a supply cache, dressed with crates or barrels; generic environment dressing, not a named canonical room. Optional, procedurally placed game adaptation; exact rooms and supplies are invented.

discoveries.label: Torch maintenance niche
discoveries.description: Wall-side niche with torch and crate dressing for variation along established rock passages, holding an optional cache. Optional, procedurally placed game adaptation; exact rooms and supplies are invented.

discoveries.label: Gym equipment alcove
discoveries.description: A generic storage alcove with gym equipment and an optional cache near the Juicer’s gym. Optional, procedurally placed game adaptation; exact rooms and supplies are invented.

discoveries.label: Narrow service passage
discoveries.description: Short side passage with pipe, drain, torch or crate dressing. It holds an optional supply cache, reconnects to its host district, and never adds a route gate. Optional, procedurally placed game adaptation; exact rooms and supplies are invented.

discoveries.label: Rubbish pocket
discoveries.description: Small rubbish-filled pocket with a cache using Hoarder/Scatterer lair visual vocabulary; not a separate nest. Optional, procedurally placed game adaptation; exact rooms and supplies are invented.

adaptationNote: Continuous 40 × 32 tactical scale: compact chambers and inferred connecting passages. The source-linked district route stays fixed. Seeds add optional chambers with varied positions, footprints, shapes, thematic anchor passages and supplies; these extra locations are inferred game adaptations, not newly discovered canonical places. Existing enemy kits stand in for Book 1 encounters; this does not run the separate boss scenarios. All required discoveries and tactical encounters unlock the exit. Atlas passage objective locks are not applied in this combat map. The playable game uses these same saved whole-object components over reusable ground and wall tiles; terrain and component footprints share canonical collision. The optional roster is a gameplay adaptation.
